primarySource.title: Driving in Thailand: Thailand Driving Guide

primaryPageChecks.notes: General tips: left-side driving; separate toll, parking and night sections inspected.
General tips: alcohol avoidance, school/community zones and crossing guidance; motorcycle-gap description is observational, not permission.
Car-rental page: inspection, photos and pre-existing damage notes. Licensing/insurance statements are not imported.
Road etiquette: normal driving, high-beam glare, right-lane cooperation, school caution and allowing overtakes.
Road etiquette: safe stopping, brake-light checks, keeping entrances clear and phone distraction. Hands-free qualification and parking context inspected.
Road etiquette: rain guidance, necessary horn use, emergency warnings and keeping left on narrow roads.
Inappropriate driving: sidewalks, tailgating, shoulders and lane straddling; numerical penalty and reverse-driving statements excluded.
Safe driving: seatbelt/helmet preparation, safe following gap, community/child caution and readiness to stop.
Condition-adjusted speed and cyclist blind-spot checks at park/community entrances. Numerical speed illustrations are not asserted by candidates.
Blind-spot definition and diagrams, lane-change warning, following-space tips; motorcycle blind spots included in illustration.
Safe motorcycle riding: equipment, secure helmets for both occupants, signals, no cutting, heavy-rain avoidance and truck clearance.
Truck guidance explicitly names car and motorcycle drivers; rear/left blind spots, turning squeeze and front stopping clearance. Numerical gap not imported.
Complete motorcycle hazard panel: fresh rain, potholes/puddles, metal plates, speed bumps, oil, gravel/sand; every distinct panel read.
Night driving: continuous headlights, greater gaps and safely parked illuminated breakdown. Numerical warning visibility is outside candidate claim.
Rain: reduce speed, enlarge gap, avoid abrupt brakes, use headlights/turn signals and avoid unnecessary hazards; flooded/curve qualifications read.
High-risk areas: yellow-light stop, curve lane/speed guidance and railway caution. Numerical rail distance and unrelated intersection/U-turn claims excluded.
Vulnerable road users: slower elderly crossings and explicit slow/stop guidance; cyclist and motorcyclist warnings also inspected.
Vehicle-law page: registered vehicles require complete equipment. Registration, red-plate, penalty claims are not taught here.
Highway page: speed-sign adherence paragraph. Engine-class numbers, right-lane minima, fines and waste rules are not asserted.
Traffic regulations: general signals, roundabout yield/path and overtaking signal/clearance; left-side exceptions and roundabout diagram inspected.
Parking: red/white prohibits stopping/parking; other curb colours and separate parking restrictions inspected to disambiguate.
Crossing guidance clearly separates pedestrian lights from vehicle lights; vehicle red requires stop, yellow prepares stop.
Pedestrian safety: slow/stop to allow crossing; parking on crossing prohibited. Numerical crossing/overtaking distances not asserted.
General prohibitions: obstruction, alcohol, impaired consciousness including drowsy flu medication. Numeric penalty not asserted.
Expressway breakdown: when still driveable move left/out of traffic and use hazards; immovable case, assistance and seatbelt context read. CAR only.
Railway: no-signal checks, approaching-train stop clear of tracks; separate emergency-vehicle give-way/left-edge subsection. Numeric distances not asserted.

decisions.notes: The general driving instruction specifies the left side; none of the other positions is the ordinary direction of travel.
The traffic-rules paragraph explicitly requires turn signals for lane changes; after-the-move signals, hazards and movement alone are not substitutes.
The page explicitly links a larger/sufficient gap to safe stopping or additional reaction time; closing the gap and ignoring brake lights contradict it.
Community guidance names small children and unexpected crossings, requires low speed and readiness to stop; horn use is not a substitute.
The environment/rain guidance requires speed reduction appropriate to road, weather and traffic; the posted maximum is not a safe target in every condition.
The text defines areas outside mirror visibility and cautions especially during lane changes; mirrors and signals cannot guarantee an empty adjacent lane.
The truck guidance explicitly addresses cars and motorcycles, warns against close following and identifies limited visibility on the left; the keyed position/gap avoids the described blind spot.
The truck guidance explicitly addresses cars and motorcycles, warns against close following and identifies limited visibility on the left; the keyed position/gap avoids the described blind spot.
The page warns of squeezing when entering a turning or reversing truck area; remaining clear is the only supported option.
The truck may have a longer stopping distance; immediate close re-entry denies the truck that space.
Night-driving guidance requires headlights continuously; hazards, empty roads and street lighting are not exemptions.
The etiquette paragraph names glare affecting both the preceding and oncoming driver; reducing high beam resolves the specified hazard.
The page explicitly links a larger/sufficient gap to safe stopping or additional reaction time; closing the gap and ignoring brake lights contradict it.
The environment/rain guidance requires speed reduction appropriate to road, weather and traffic; the posted maximum is not a safe target in every condition.
The page explicitly links a larger/sufficient gap to safe stopping or additional reaction time; closing the gap and ignoring brake lights contradict it.
Rain guidance expressly warns that abrupt braking can cause skidding; smooth planned braking is the sole controlled response.
The rain page explicitly combines headlights, appropriate turn signals and avoiding unnecessary hazards because direction becomes confusing.
The curve paragraph combines lower speed with staying in the designated lane and avoiding overtaking/abrupt stops; only the keyed plan does so.
The phone paragraph identifies distraction and directs an extended interaction to a safe parking spot; texting while moving remains unsafe.
The primary page explicitly advises avoiding driving under alcohol influence; slowing, familiar routes and fresh air do not provide a safe alternative to other transport.
The page explicitly gives drowsiness after flu medicine as impaired consciousness; avoiding driving addresses the impairment.
The page prohibits driving/parking on sidewalks and reserves them for pedestrians; an apparently empty sidewalk is not a queue bypass.
The page prohibits using the shoulder as ordinary travel space and describes its emergency function; congestion does not change the stated rule.
The inappropriate-behaviour paragraph forbids straddling/weaving across dividers; ordinary travel stays within a lane.
The horn paragraph allows necessary accident warnings or emergencies and discourages excessive/intimidating use; only the danger warning fits.
The paragraph explicitly combines reducing speed and keeping left in opposing traffic; claiming the centre or moving right contradicts it.
The vehicle-light subsection explicitly says vehicles must stop on red; the pedestrian-signal subsection is separately labelled and was not confused with it.
The page says slow and stop before the designated line; the stem expressly establishes sufficient safe stopping distance.
The roundabout subsection says yield to traffic already circulating. CAR wording needs a grammatical improvement, but A is the sole supported traffic group.
The same subsection specifies following the designated circulating path without cutting across; counterflow and shortcuts contradict it.
Crossing guidance requires stopping to allow safe passage; the elderly-person variant is separately supported by the slower-crossing warning and stop instruction.
The crossing rules explicitly prohibit parking on the crossing; hazards or remaining nearby do not provide an exception.
The parking paragraph expressly forbids blocking entrances/exits; a brief stay, phone number or closed gate does not satisfy keeping access clear.
The emergency subsection requires stopping or pulling toward the left edge; staying in the way or following closely contradicts it.

The railway subsection requires stopping before an approaching train and avoiding the tracks; only a clear waiting position is supported. The scenario does not purport to teach the full numerical clearance rule.
The railway subsection expressly calls for extra caution, left/right checks and proceeding only when safe in the absence of warning signals.
The overtaking paragraphs require signalling, clearance and no obstruction; desired speed, horn use or mere observation by another driver do not establish a safe pass.
The etiquette paragraph directs giving space/slowing or moving left and forbids a speed competition; cooperative room is the sole safe option.
The coloured-curb table explicitly says white/red means no stopping or parking; this was read with the separate white/yellow and white/black entries.

The speed-sign instruction explicitly says adhere to the indicated limit; CAR grammar can improve, but the lower current-road sign is the sole supported choice. No numerical or engine-class claim is asserted.
Safe-driving guidance recommends fastening before driving every time to reduce injury; a short quiet trip does not remove the stated safety benefit.

CAR equipment completeness is supported by registered-vehicle guidance; motorcycle brake repair is supported by the specific motorcycle readiness checklist. Deferring faults or substituting horn/warnings does not correct them.

The motorcycle hazard panel identifies slippery metal plates and advises reduced speed and firm handlebar grip; accelerating or sharp leaning/braking contradicts it.
The motorcycle pothole panel names puddles as a risk and specifies low speed, firm handlebars and avoiding sudden brakes.
The oil-spill panel advises avoiding spills; the stem provides a safe clear alternative, so the avoidance answer does not invite an abrupt unsafe swerve.
The gravel/sand panel identifies loss-of-control risk near construction and calls for extreme care; treating it as clean asphalt or weaving is unsupported.
The speed-bump panel advises lower speed in accordance with signs and stable posture; jumping or last-moment braking is unsupported.
The motorcycle riding subsection explicitly says not to cut between cars and not to change lanes abruptly; only the predictable-path option follows that guidance.
The motorcycle subsection advises avoiding riding if possible in heavy rain because visibility/control worsen; the optional journey can safely wait.
The page prohibits obstructing traffic; choosing a permitted stopping place clear of the traffic route directly addresses the scenario.
